content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

The draft specification is ready for review:

- [Bookmark Manager specification](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md)
- [Quality checklist](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/checklists/requirements.md) — all checks passed
- Feature directory: `specs/001-bookmark-manager`

The proposed first release is a single-user bookmark manager with manual saving, notes, tags, search, filtering, sorting, editing, deletion, and duplicate warnings. Accounts, synchronization, sharing, folders, browser extensions, and import/export are excluded for now.

Please approve the specification or tell me what you’d like changed. Once approved, I’ll move to the implementation-plan gate.

Thanks for putting this together — it's clear and easy to read. A lot of it matches what I pictured: saving links, tags, search, filtering, sorting, editing, deleting. But reading it as if I were using it day to day, several things are missing or work differently than I'd expect, so I can't approve it as-is yet.

A few things really matter to me:

- **Saving should do the busy work for me.** I saw that I'd have to type in a title myself, and that grabbing the page's details automatically is left out. That's not what I want — when I paste a link, I expect it to go fetch the page's title, its little icon, and ideally a short description or preview, so I don't have to type anything. I'd still want to be able to tweak that title or description before and after saving, but the app should fill it in first.

- **Saving the same link twice.** You've got it warning me and letting me keep both copies. Honestly I don't want two copies — if I save a link I already saved, I'd expect it to just take me to the existing one so I can update it. Preventing duplicates matters more to me than being allowed to keep them.

- **A "read later" idea.** I often save things I haven't read yet. I'd want to mark a bookmark as unread and then have a way to look at just my unread ones, and mark them read once I'm done.

- **Archiving, separate from deleting.** Delete should be permanent, yes. But I also want to be able to tuck a bookmark away — get it out of my main list without losing it — and pull up an "archived" list later. Right now there's only delete.

- **Notes with a bit of formatting.** Plain text is a little thin. I'd like my notes to support simple formatting (headings, lists, links) and show up nicely formatted when I read them.

- **Smarter search.** Case-insensitive search is good. But I'd also want to search by tag with a shorthand, combine conditions (this AND that, one OR another, excluding something), and search an exact phrase in quotes.

- **Handling many at once.** When I'm tidying up, I'd like to select several bookmarks and do one action to all of them — tag them, mark read/unread, archive, or delete — including everything currently matching my search or filter.

- **Saving a search I use often.** If I've set up a search with certain tags included and others excluded, I'd like to save that combination and reuse it later.

- **Bringing my existing bookmarks in, and getting them out.** I already have bookmarks elsewhere. I'd want to import them from the standard bookmarks file and be able to export mine back out too. Leaving that out would be a real gap for me.

- **A few display preferences.** Being able to set my default sort order, how many items show, and text size would make it feel like mine.

I'm fine leaving out accounts, syncing across devices, sharing with other people, and folders for now — those aren't important to me yet. Could you fold the items above into the spec and bring it back?

content:
The revised specification is ready:

- [Revised Bookmark Manager specification](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md)
- [Updated quality checklist](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/checklists/requirements.md) — all checks pass
- Feature directory: `specs/001-bookmark-manager`

All requested capabilities are now included. I also made these explicit defaults for review:

- Imported browser folders become tags.
- New and imported bookmarks start unread.
- URL fragments and superficial URL variations do not create duplicates.
- Imported duplicates never overwrite existing details.
- Notes support headings, lists, and links.
- Export uses browser-compatible HTML and warns about details that format cannot preserve.
- Default display is newest-first, 25 items per page, standard text size.

Please approve this revision or flag any further changes. Once approved, I’ll prepare the implementation plan for the next review gate.

This looks great — you've captured everything I asked for, and reading through it I recognize how I'd actually use it. Automatic details on save with the ability to edit, saving a repeat link taking me to the one I already have, the read-later and archive flows, formatted notes, the more powerful search with tags and exact phrases and combining conditions, saving searches I reuse, acting on many at once, bringing my bookmarks in and out, and the display preferences — that's the picture I had in my head.

Your defaults all sound sensible to me too: turning imported folders into tags, new items starting unread, ignoring trivial address differences, not overwriting my existing entries on import, and the newest-first / 25-per-page / normal-text defaults. Good.

The specification is approved. Please go ahead and prepare the implementation plan for the next gate.

The plan selects a single Next.js/React application, SQLite with full-text search, transactional bulk operations, and strongly guarded metadata fetching. Node 24 is an active LTS release, and React 19.3 is the current documented version. ([Node.js releases](https://nodejs.org/en/about/previous-releases), [React versions](https://react.dev/versions))

The speckit-plan workflow drove the research, data model, contracts, security boundaries, and end-to-end validation design. No unresolved clarifications or constitution conflicts remain.

- US3 Read/archive workflow: 6
- US4 Search and saved searches: 9

Every story has an independent test checkpoint. Task IDs are sequential from T001–T080, and every task follows the required checkbox, ID, story label, and exact-file-path format.

The suggested initial MVP is US1: safely retrieve page details, allow manual editing, save the bookmark, and reopen it. US2–US4 then complete the reliable daily-use experience.

Please approve the task list or request changes. Implementation will begin only after approval.

I've had a good look and a poke around, and this is exactly what we agreed on. Everything I care about is there and behaving the way I pictured:

- Saving a link pulls in details and keeps my edits, with a fallback icon when there isn't one.
- Saving a link I already have — even with different capitalization or a trailing `#` bit — takes me back to the existing one instead of making a second copy. That was important to me and it works.
- Read-later, archive, and restore are all present, and new items start unread.
- Search handles tag shorthand and exact phrases, and shows me how it read my query.
- Saved searches, bulk selection, rich formatted notes, and my display preferences are all in place.
- I can export my collection to a normal browser bookmarks file (tags and all) and import one back in.

It also feels calm and clear to use, which I appreciate. I'm happy with it — this is what I wanted. Accepted.

I do have a couple of ideas for down the road (like keeping a saved copy of a page in case it disappears), but those are new wishes for a later round, not anything missing from what we agreed. Thank you for the careful work.
